mstts:express-as.prosody:
Let’s talk about something truly powerful— the power of story and community.
As time goes on, the story of loss and resilience doesn’t just stay with you. It becomes a bridge, reaching out to others. More and more, you notice that everyone’s carrying some kind of invisible wound. And when you share your own story, it’s not just for you—it’s a real gift to anyone who’s struggling quietly.
Maybe you find yourself speaking to a group, or writing, or even making art. These become ways to connect, to offer hope and let people know they’re not alone.
There’s this memory that stands out—a young person, sitting quietly at the back of a packed room, listening to a story about finding purpose right in the middle of pain. After the story, they come up to you. They’re a little hesitant, but you can see hope in their eyes. They open up about their own struggles.
It’s in moments like this that you realize—being vulnerable, telling your truth without sugarcoating anything, that’s what really brings people together. When you share honestly about your life, you’re giving others permission to do the same.
Community starts to mean something deeper. It’s not just about getting support—it’s about giving it, too. There’s this real sense of belonging that comes from walking beside others, sharing not just the good times, but also the tough ones. The relationships you build here are honest, full of empathy, and grounded in showing up for each other—even when things get messy.
And as you keep going, advocacy and education start to feel like a natural next step. You want to challenge the way people think about disability, to push for better accessibility and real inclusion. It’s about reminding everyone that every life has value. This isn’t about asking for pity—it’s about inviting others to see the richness and complexity in lives that look a little different from what’s considered “normal.”
Through all of this, sharing—whether it’s through words, through art, or just by being present—becomes a powerful way to turn pain into purpose. The story you carry isn’t just about surviving anymore. It’s about creating spaces where others can discover hope and feel like they belong.
